t: From a blank sheet to your first part for the 3D printer, in five minutes, with no account and nothing to install. layerling is a design program for 3D printing that runs right in your browser. You build a part from simple shapes, cut holes into it, round the edges and send it to your slicer. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for. What you build stays on your computer. The start page of layerling: "Create new 3D design" at the top, your designs and the quick guide below.

Open layerling.com. On the start page click 「新しい3Dデザインを作成」. The editor opens with an empty workplane, the grid on which everything takes shape. If you already have a file to continue with, use 「デザインを開く、またはジオメトリを読み込む」. That works for layerling designs (.lyl) as well as STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP or SVG files. All your designs later appear on the start page with a preview picture. They are kept in your browser's storage and saved automatically after every change, so there is no save button. layerling takes no responsibility for designs kept in the browser. A browser can fail, or a browser update can cause problems, so back up your designs from time to time with 「すべてバックアップ」 on the start page, or save them as files. A backup comes back with 「バックアップを戻す」. How to pack designs into a file and pass them on is covered in Files and saving. If you would like a reminder, switch on 「タブを閉じる前にたずねる」 in the settings (the cogwheel in the ribbon): the browser then asks before a tab with an open design is closed or reloaded.

The editor with its areas labelled: the ribbon on top, the view cube on the left with the view bar below it, the status message and the object list beside them, the properties of the selected shape on the right. On top is the ribbon. It is sorted by task: 「クリップボード」, 「履歴」, 「シェイプ」, 「表示」, 「結合」, 「変形」, 「配置」 and 「ファイル」; 「ヘルプ」 sits above it in the title row, and the house beside the tabs leads back to the start page. When the window is too narrow for all groups, the ones used least fold into one button under their name, with a small arrow in the group's colour hanging beneath it: point at it or tap it, and its tools open beneath it. Folded 「履歴」 is the exception: its button is 「元に戻す」 itself, and only the arrow beneath it opens 「やり直す」 and the rest. The pin at the top right, left of the magnifying glass, keeps all groups open instead. Hover over an icon to see its name, a greyed-out one too; 「インタラクティブヘルプ」 (the question mark under 「ヘルプ」, or Shift+F1) explains any of them with a click and leads to its section of this guide. Wherever you see a small question mark, for example in a shape's properties, in the shape library or in the tool windows, it leads straight to the matching chapter of this guide. The 「変形」 group is divided into four sections, each named above its tools: 「ミラーとパターン」, 「分割と成形」, 「エッジと壁」 and 「表面」. A greyed-out icon also says what it is waiting for, such as 「ボディを 1 つ選択してください」, or 「選択範囲はロックされています。先にロックを解除してください」. Can't find a tool? Press Ctrl+K and type its name; an empty design reminds you of this at the bottom of the view. In the middle lies the workplane. This is where you place shapes, pull them into form and see the result. On the right is the properties panel of the selected shape: colour, dimensions, position and whatever else makes up the shape. Typing numbers is more exact than dragging. On the left is the view bar with the view cube above it. They move you around the scene, more in View and workplane. Beside the view bar the object list opens (Ctrl+U), with every shape of the design. More in Select and arrange. To the right of the view cube the status message appears when layerling has something to tell you, such as what a tool expects from you next. When there is nothing to say, it is not there. Tool windows open over the workplane when you start a tool such as fillet, pattern or hollow. Drag one aside by its title bar when it covers something. At the very top you switch between 「3Dエディター」 and 「スケッチ」, rename the design and choose language and colour scheme.

h: The buttons around the work area
t: Hover over a button to see its name. If you are not sure what a button does, click 「インタラクティブヘルプ」 in the 「ヘルプ」 area (Shift+F1) and then the button. These are the ones asked about most.

「貼り付け」 (Ctrl+V) adds what you copied with 「コピー」 to the design. 「複製」 copies and pastes in one step. A paste puts each part a little beside where it was. Parts that come from another program can land far from the plate, and for those there is 「まん中に貼り付けて落とす」 in the settings, under 「外観」: a paste then sets the parts together in the middle of the workplane and drops them onto it.
「削除」 (Delete) removes the selected shapes. 「元に戻す」 brings them back.
「グループ解除」 (Ctrl+Shift+G) takes the selected group apart again into the shapes it was made of.
「ワークスペース設定」 opens the settings of the work area: unit, size of the plate, printer, grid, colours, light and more. More in View and workplane.
「テーマ」 at the very top chooses how layerling looks: as your system, light, dark or graphite.
「デザインの名前を変更」: the pencil beside the name at the very top. Type the new name and press Enter.
The name of the design (「デザイン名」) stands at the very top. Click it, type, and Enter keeps the name.
「表示オプション」, the arrow beside the eye icon, holds what you can show or hide: the list of objects, everything you hid, the notes and the overhangs of the print. More in Select and arrange.
「選択を非表示」 (Ctrl+H) hides the selected shapes. They stay in the design and in the object list; 「表示オプション」 shows them again.
「コマンドを検索（Ctrl+K）」: type what you look for, a tool, a shape or a setting, and click the result.
「ビューバーを非表示」 folds the view bar on the left away and gives the work area more room; 「ビューバーを表示」 brings them back.
「スナップグリッド」, at the bottom of the properties, is the step that moving and resizing snaps to. Beside it the small switch mm | in changes the unit. More in View and workplane.
The switch mm | in beside 「スナップグリッド」 changes the unit, the plate's grid and the snap step, for this design.

At the foot of the window: 「プロジェクトを支援」 leads to the page where you can support the project; 「ユーザーガイド」 opens this guide; 「ディスカッション」 leads to the place for questions, ideas and bug reports (the discussions on GitHub, in German the forum of drucktipps3d); 「バグ報告」 makes a ZIP for a bug report; 「詳細はGitHubで」 leads to the project on GitHub, and the version number opens the release notes. The links to the imprint and the privacy policy belong to whoever runs the copy of layerling you use.

As an example, we build a cube with a hole. Click 「シェイプを追加」 in the ribbon and pick 「直方体」. The shape now hangs on your mouse pointer. A click on the workplane sets it down. On the right, set the dimensions, for example 40 mm long, 40 mm wide and 20 mm high. Place a 「円柱」 in the middle the same way, 14 mm across and 30 mm high. It should be taller than the cube so it reaches all the way through. Select the cylinder and click 「穴」 on the right. It turns see-through: the solid has become a tool that takes material away. Select both shapes and click 「グループ化」. The cube now has a hole. The cylinder is a hole and sticks out of the top of the cube. After grouping, the cube has a bore. This is how bores, slots and pockets are made. The chapter Solids and holes explains it in detail.

When you open layerling again after an update, a card on the start page lists what has been added since you were last here: every version since then, the newest first. After a long absence you scroll down inside the card. Below them, 「以前のバージョンを表示」 adds the versions from before your last visit too. Close it with 「わかりました」 and it stays away until the next update. 「新機能は？」 in the footer of the start page shows the latest additions again at any time. The browser remembers the last version you saw, and nothing about you leaves it. On a copy of layerling on your own computer or server, the notice "Update available" has a button, 「プレビュー: このアップデートで何が変わる？」, that lists what the update brings before you install it. The list is fetched from GitHub only when you press the button.

When your part is done, click 「エクスポート」, choose STL or 3MF and download the file. Open it in your slicer, for example Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer or Cura. If you choose your printer in the settings, you can see while building whether the part fits on the print bed. More in Printing. Tip: If you come from Tinkercad you will find your way quickly: plate, shapes, solid and hole, group, align and mirror work almost the same. What is new is mostly chamfer and fillet, hollowing, threads and sketches. Your own Tinkercad designs can come along too, see Files, saving and sharing.
Moving around the scene, looking straight on, and placing new shapes on any surface you like.

With the mouse: What you do What happens drag with the right button rotate the view click the right button on a body, a menu with the most used commands: duplicate, hole or solid, group, hide, lock, delete and more; on empty space Paste and Select all drag with the middle button move the view mouse wheel zoom in and out hold Ctrl / Cmd and drag with the left button also moves the view (on a MacBook trackpad: hold Cmd, press and drag); on a Mac, holding Control instead turns the view, as Control-click is the Mac's right click double-click on empty workplane or beside the plate moves the view so that the spot comes to the middle; the view then turns around it How fast the wheel zooms is set with 「ズーム速度」 in the settings, under 「外観」: a slider from 1 to 14, 5 to begin with. It sets the wheel and the trackpad only: the buttons and the keys + and − always zoom in the same small steps. One notch of a mouse wheel zooms alike in every browser, a trackpad zooms with how far you stroke. Mouse buttons as in your slicer. If you are used to Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer, set 「マウスのボタン」 in the settings, under 「外観」, to 「Bambu StudioやOrcaSlicerと同じ」. A left drag on empty space then turns the view, the right button shifts it as the middle one does, and Shift with a left drag draws the selection box. A drag on a body still moves it, and a short right click still opens the menu. In a sketch the right button shifts the view too. 3D mouse. A SpaceMouse or another 3D mouse turns, shifts and zooms the 3D view: push the cap away to zoom in, slide it to shift the view, tilt it to tilt the view and twist it to turn the view round. In the settings, under 「外観」, click 「3Dマウスをつなぐ」 and choose the device in the window the browser opens; it remembers the choice, so this is needed only once. This works in Chrome and Edge, which can reach such devices; Firefox and Safari cannot. If a direction feels the wrong way round, tick it under the button: shifting sideways, shifting up and down, zooming, tilting or twisting. On a tablet or phone, two fingers zoom (spread and pinch) and move the view (slide together). One finger on empty space turns the view, and a tap there clears the selection; on a shape or a handle it works on the design, just like the left mouse button. To turn the view with a finger that starts on a shape too, switch on 「1本指でビューを回転」 in the view bar. That switch shows on devices with a touch screen. A graphics tablet with a pen behaves like a mouse: the tip is the left button, the barrel button on the pen the right one, for turning the view and for the menu. The tablet's hotkeys can be set in its driver to layerling's keyboard shortcuts. On a tablet, work with a stylus if you can. Its tip is far finer than a fingertip and does not cover what you aim at, so small points, thin lines and handles in a sketch, measuring points and edges are hit exactly, and longer work is less tiring. layerling already lets a finger reach a little further to points, lines, handles and edges than a mouse pointer does, but a stylus remains the more precise way. This holds for a pen that the tablet knows as a pen (an S Pen, an Apple Pencil and the like). A plain stylus with a rubber tip counts as a finger for the screen and is not finer than one. There is no right mouse button on a tablet: hold a finger still on a shape or on empty space for half a second, and the menu opens that a right click opens, with Select all on empty space. Select multiple in the same menu stands in for Shift on a tablet: each tap on a body then adds it to the selection or takes it out again, until you tap empty space or press Esc; a finger on empty space still turns the view. The handles around a selected shape can be caught by a finger from a little beside them.

The cube in the top left shows where you are looking. A click on one of its sides jumps to the straight view from top, bottom, front, back, left or right. A click on a corner of the cube looks at the model diagonally from that corner, and a click near an edge looks from that edge, between two sides; the spot lights up while the pointer is on it. The number keys 1 to 6 give the straight views too. Hold Shift with them and the view also zooms to the selection, as Shift+F does. Drag the cube to turn the view around, just like dragging with the right mouse button. With nothing selected, the arrow keys turn the view as well: 15° a press, 90° with Shift. They turn the model the way they point - → turns its front to the right, ↑ tilts its front upwards. With Ctrl held, the arrows slide the view across the screen instead: a tenth of the picture a press, half of it with Shift as well. The model moves the way they point. If something is selected, the arrows move it; click on empty space first to turn the view. On a touch screen this works with one finger, without switching on 「1本指でビューを回転」.

At the left edge is a narrow bar. From the top: 「ホームビュー」 brings the whole scene back into view. The key is Home; F does it too when nothing is selected. 「選択したものを中央に表示」 zooms to the selection (F or Shift+F); with nothing selected it brings the whole scene into view, as F does. 「拡大」 and 「縮小」 zoom step by step, as do the keys + and −. 「平行投影表示」 switches to a flat view in which parallel edges stay parallel. For measuring and lining up edges that is often more comfortable than the perspective view. O switches back and forth, and a second click returns. 「2つ目のビューを開く」 opens a second view of the design in a window of its own, described below. A second click closes it. 「Show scrollbars」 puts a scrollbar along the bottom of the view and one down its right edge. Drag a bar to slide the view smoothly, click an arrow at its end to move it a little (hold it to keep going), or click beside the bar to move by most of the view. Nothing turns, and unlike the arrow keys the bars work while a part is selected - handy close up on small details. A second click hides them; 「スクロールバーを表示してエディターを開始」 in the settings decides whether a design opens with them. This browser also remembers the switch. 「作業平面を非表示」 (the eye over a grid) hides the plate with its grid, so you can look at the underside of a design from below. Only the view changes: new shapes still land on the workplane. A second click shows it again. 「作業平面を配置」, the tape measure and the framing square are tools of their own, covered below and in Measuring and notes. The small arrow at the very top of the bar hides it if it gets in the way. That same button, dragged, moves the bar anywhere in the editor, in a sketch too; a double click puts it back. The 3D preview of a revolved sketch moves by its title in the same way. A design opens the way you left it: the angle, zoom and position of the view are kept with it in this browser, so you continue where you stopped, also after going Home or closing the page. A saved file (.lyl) carries the view along, so it opens in it elsewhere too. The view is not part of the undo history. You can also keep four views of your own in each design. Shift+7, Shift+8, Shift+9 or Shift+0 saves the view exactly as it is - angle, position, zoom, and flat or perspective - under that key, and the key alone (7, 8, 9 or 0) brings it back. A message at the bottom confirms the save; saving again under the same key replaces the view. Like the view above, the saved views stay with the design in this browser and travel in a saved file (.lyl), and they are not part of the undo history.

h: A second view in its own window
t: 「2つ目のビューを開く」 opens a window that shows the same design through a camera of its own, so you can see it from two sides at once - from the front, say, while you work from above. Every change you make in the editor shows there straight away; the design is only changed in the main window, and the handles stay there too. In the second window the mouse and the view cube turn its view as they do here, and so do the keys: 1 to 6, F, Home, O, + and −, the arrow keys to turn and Ctrl with the arrows to slide. F there zooms to what is selected in the editor. The design's four saved views work there too: 7, 8, 9 and 0 bring them back, and Shift with one of these keys saves that window's view under it - for both windows. Its own view bar has 「ホームビュー」, 「選択したものを中央に表示」, 「拡大」, 「縮小」, 「平行投影表示」 and 「作業平面を非表示」, and they act on that window alone. The window opens where you left it, at the same size, and closes with the editor. On phones and tablets the button is not shown.

「断面表示」, the last button in the bar (the cut tool), cuts the view open along a plane so you can check walls, cavities and parts that fit into each other. Nothing is cut for real: the design, its files and every export stay whole. Where the plane goes through a solid, the cut is filled with the colour of the body a little darker, and a hole inside it stays empty, so you can tell solid from hollow; the filled face appears a moment after the plane stops moving. Under 「切断面」 you choose how the cut looks: 「ハッチング」, the start, hatches it like a drawing, and a body that lies inside another is hatched the other way, so the two stand apart; 「塗りつぶし」 fills it plain; 「開く」 leaves it open, and you look into the skin of the body. The choice holds for every design. Choose the axis the plane stands across: X (width), Y (depth) or Z (height), as in the position fields. The plane starts in the middle of your design. 「軸の基準」 sets what these axes follow. 「デザイン」 takes the design's axes. 「作業面」 takes the workplane's: Z then cuts parallel to it, X and Y square to it, and the position counts from its origin. With the workplane on a sloped face you cut parallel to that face, and the cut moves along when you move the workplane. 「視点」 turns the plane to face the screen: it takes away what lies in front, and the slider pushes it deeper into the design along your line of sight, for example to reach a buried part and click it. After turning the view, click it again and the cut follows the new view. 「粗調整」 moves the plane across the whole design, 「微調整」 moves it a little either side of where it stands, for tenths of a millimetre. You can also type the position. The button beside the axes shows the other side of the cut, 「中央」 puts the plane back in the middle, and 「切断面を表示」 hides the blue plane. You can click and select what the cut lays open, inner walls included. 「ここに作業平面」 puts the workplane on the cut. It lies on the plane of the section and faces out of the body that stays, like the face a cut leaves. If you then switch to the sketch, it starts exactly there, and the faint outline shows the cut, which you can draw along and snap to. That is how you sketch a lid that fits the cavity you opened with the section, for example. The button beside the axes chooses which side stays, and with it which way the workplane faces. You put the workplane back on the base plate as usual. 「断面からスケッチ」 starts a new sketch right on the cut, with the cut's outlines already in it as lines: a hole comes in as a true circle, a rounded corner as an arc. Change them, delete what you don't need, draw more, and finish: the body grows out of the cut towards the side that is cut away, so a part that has to fit another one, such as a lid, an insert or a gasket, starts from that part's own outline. The button beside the axes chooses that side. As for the SVG, only visible bodies count and holes are already taken off. 「計測」 measures right on the cut: the outline shows in blue, and two clicks on it give the distance, plus its parts along the plane's two axes. Both points snap to the outline, corners first. When the second click lands anywhere on the opposite wall, it snaps square to the first point - so you read wall thickness, gaps and clearance without aiming exactly. A third click starts the next measurement, Esc ends measuring. Moving the plane clears the measurement. On a round outline, such as the cut through a cylinder or a hole, a small cross marks the centre and the centre snaps too. Click a point on the circle, then go near the point across from it: the second click lands exactly across the centre, and the number reads Ø, the diameter. From the centre to a point on the circle you get R, the radius. 「断面をSVGに」 saves the outlines on the cutting plane as an SVG at 1:1, for a laser, a plotter, a template or a gasket. An X cut is seen from the right, a Y cut from the front, a Z cut from above. As in the export, only visible bodies go in, holes are already taken off, and bodies of the same colour are joined into one outline. Each colour stays its own path without a fill, so laser software keeps them apart as layers. The tool window hangs on its button. If it covers something, drag it by its title bar anywhere on the workplane; it opens there next time too. Double-click the title bar or drop it at the button to put it back. The X and Esc close the tool window; with a measuring running, Esc ends it first. The cut stays until you switch it off with 「断面表示オン」, click its button in the bar while the window is open, or go back to the design overview. While it is on, its button stays highlighted. Anything you place on the side that is cut away only shows once you switch the cut off. A tablet has no Esc, so there the tool window has two more buttons: 「戻る」 ends the measuring if one is running and otherwise closes the tool window, and 「閉じる」 closes the tool window in one step. A computer does not show them.

New shapes align with the workplane. At first that is the base plate with the grid. But you can put it on any surface, to place something on a side or a sloped face. Press W or click 「作業平面を配置」. Move the mouse over a face of a body. It lights up. A click puts the workplane there. Everything you add now sits on that face. Click on the empty plate instead, and the workplane lies flat at the spot you clicked, on the snap grid. New shapes and a finished sketch, a revolved one too, then appear there rather than in the middle of the plate. While the workplane lies flat on the plate like this, the plate shows only its outline: two grids in the same plane would make a flickering pattern. On a face the origin of the workplane otherwise snaps to the grid. Click close to a corner of the face and it sits exactly on that corner. Close to an edge it lies on the edge, and the grid lines up with it; that is how you choose the angle of the grid on purpose. Without a corner or an edge, the grid on a lying face runs parallel to the body, so on a turned box it is turned with it. A click beside the plate or Esc returns the workplane to the base plate. Quicker still is 「作業平面をベースプレートに戻す」: the button with the downward arrow sits in the view bar below the eye while the workplane lies on a face. Shift+W puts it directly on the currently selected face. Alt+W puts it back on the base plate at any time, whether something is selected or not. If you hold Shift while clicking, the plane points the other way. While a workplane sits on a face, an eye appears next to 「作業平面を配置」. It hides the workplane without dropping it, for a clear look at the design: new shapes still land on that face, and rotating still turns about it. A click on the eye shows it again, and so does setting a new workplane. A box's size handles follow a workplane that stands on one of its sides too: the corner and edge handles lie on that face, and each one changes the box's own width, length or height that runs along it. The handle in the middle of the face changes the size across it. To look straight at the workplane, press P or click 「作業平面を正面から見る」 next to 「作業平面を配置」 in the view bar. The view turns until you see the workplane square, from the side new shapes grow towards, with its origin in the middle. On the base plate that is the view from above.

When a design holds more than one plate can print, a box with its lid and inserts for example, it can have several build plates. Click 「Build plates」 in the 「配置」 group, or choose 「Onto plate…」 in the menu of a right click on a body. A bar appears at the foot of the view with one button per plate; the number on it says how many bodies stand on the plate. Every plate is as large as the workplane, and the plates lie side by side to the right of the first one, 20 mm apart. A body belongs to the plate the middle of its footprint stands on, so dragging it across puts it on the other plate. A design holds up to 12 plates. A click on a plate in the bar looks at it, and new shapes and imported files then land on it. 「Show all plates」 looks at all of them. A double click on a plate, or 「Rename plate」, gives it a name such as "Lid", which is written on the plate. 「Move plate left」 and 「Move plate right」 change the order, the bodies moving with their plate. 「Remove plate (its bodies go onto the first plate)」 takes the active plate away; its bodies go onto the first plate at the same spot. 「Arrange on plates」 lays the selected bodies, or all of them, out row by row on the plates, the largest first, 5 mm apart, and adds plates while they are needed. A body larger than a plate stays where it is. With a printer chosen, every body is checked against its own plate, and the build height counts from the lowest body on that plate. A plate with a body that does not fit shows its number in red. In the properties, X counts from the middle of the body's own plate. The export window then offers 「Plates」: all plates in one file, side by side as in the design; one file per plate, packed in a ZIP (STL, 3MF and OBJ); or a single plate, set where the first plate is. A slicer opens every file as one plate, so to print the plates one after another, take the files per plate. Moving bodies between plates and arranging them can be undone; adding, naming, ordering and removing plates is kept with the design but not undone.

The grid shows the size of the plate. At the bottom right is the snap step: moving and scaling snap in steps of that size, for example 1 mm. Make it smaller for fine work and larger for rough arranging. 「グリッドにスナップ」 in the ribbon moves the selected shapes afterwards onto the nearest grid crossing. While moving, shapes also snap to other shapes, see Selecting and arranging. Without the mouse: Alt+1 to Alt+0 pick that entry of the menu (Alt+1 turns snapping off), and , and . make the step one size finer or coarser. This works in a sketch too. A short click with the middle mouse button, without moving the mouse, opens the snap step menu right at the pointer, in a sketch too; holding the middle button and dragging still moves the view. Tip: Stop rotating the view when you fit parts together exactly. Use the number keys to go to the straight view from top or front and press O for the flat display. Then you see at once whether two edges are really flush.

The cogwheel in the title row (「ワークスペース設定」) opens the settings. On the left are five areas: 「外観」, 「計測」, 「作業平面」, 「シェイプの初期値」 and 「履歴」. A change counts at once. 「初期値にする」 at the bottom saves the current settings as the default, so that a new design starts with them. A file you open brings its own settings; 「自分の初期値を使う」 next to it puts your saved colours, grid and the rest on the open design, keeping its units. If your default has a printer, that printer comes along with its plate size; without one the design keeps its plate and printer. 「設定を閉じる」 at the top right closes the window. This part goes through the settings one by one. 「Export settings」 next to it saves the settings of the window in a file (layerling-settings-<date>.json): the colours, grid, shadows, camera and shape defaults, together with the theme, toolbar size, view cube corner, shape colours and the play of each printer. On another computer, or after the browser lost its data, 「Import settings」 reads the file again: it becomes your default for new designs and goes onto the open design like 「自分の初期値を使う」. Your own keys from the keyboard shortcuts go along too.

h: Appearance: theme, toolbar and view cube
t: 「テーマ」 sets the colour scheme of the whole program: 「システム」 follows your computer, the others are 「ライト」, 「ダーク」 and 「グラファイト（中間色のダーク）」. You can also change it at the top right of the editor. 「コントロールのサイズ」 makes the buttons of the ribbon on top, its shape menu, the view bar on the left and the properties panel on the right smaller or larger: 「小」, 「中」 (as it always was) or 「大」. Small leaves more room for the workplane on a laptop; large is easier to hit on a big screen or with a finger. With large buttons the groups of the ribbon go onto a second row when the window is too narrow for them. The size sits in the 「Ribbon」 tab of the settings, is kept in this browser and holds for every design. 「シェイプをカラーで表示」 puts the colour a new shape starts with on the pictures of the shape library (the colour of its kind, or the one you saved with 「初期値として保存」). Switch it off if you prefer grey pictures; your browser remembers the choice. 「ビュー方向キューブの位置」 puts the view cube in another corner of the workplane: 「左上」 (as it always was), 「右上」, 「左下」 or 「右下」. In any corner but the top left, the view bar moves up into the spot the cube left. In the bottom right the cube stands just above the 「スナップグリッド」 control. While the properties of a shape are open on the right, a cube on the right steps to the left of them. The corner is kept in this browser and holds for every design. On a narrow window, such as a phone, the setting is hidden and the cube stays in the top left.

「Buttons in the ribbon」 takes the groups and buttons you never use out of the ribbon. Click a group to open its list: 「Show this group」 takes the whole group out, the tick next to a button just that button. 「Show all」 brings everything back. A group with no button left disappears and the others move up, so more of the ribbon fits in one row. What you take out only leaves the ribbon: the command search (Ctrl+K) still finds it, and its key still runs it. The arrows next to a group move it up or down the list, and so along the ribbon; 「Reset order」 brings back the order it came with. The arrows beside a button move it the same way inside its group; in 「変形」 it stays within its named section. The Shapes group and Help always stay, and Shapes keeps its place after the first two groups. The choice is kept in this browser and goes into the file of 「Export settings」. It applies to the 3D editor; the sketch has a bar of its own.

「高速モード」 is for slower computers. It turns off shadows, edge lines on all bodies and the camera's inertia, and draws the view at screen resolution only. Your own settings are kept for later, and the switches it overrides say 「高速モードではオフ」 while it is on. More about what helps on a slow computer is under "When layerling feels slow" below.

h: Appearance: colours of the work area and the sketch
t: The colours of the work area are set under 「外観」: 「ウィンドウの背景（ライトテーマ）」 and 「グリッドの下の作業平面（ライトテーマ）」 for the light theme (the dark themes keep their own), next to the grid colour under 「作業平面」. Each colour is a button that shows the colour. A click opens a small window with the colour field, a row of ready colours, a field for the hex value and an arrow that puts the colour back to what layerling started with. Enter takes a typed hex value, and so does a click outside the window. The sketch view has its own colours: 「スケッチ: ウィンドウの背景（ライトテーマ）」 for the window round the sheet, 「スケッチ: グリッドの下の領域（ライトテーマ）」 for the sheet under the grid, and 「スケッチ: グリッドの色（ライトテーマ）」, all for the light theme. 「スケッチを作業領域と同じにする」 takes over the work area's three colours in one click. 「クラシックな外観」 sets the work area up as Tinkercad shows it: white ground, a pale blue millimetre grid with a darker line every centimetre, black edge lines, light from above with soft shadows. Every value can still be changed on its own afterwards. All of them start as layerling always looked, and what suits you depends on your monitor. The settings under Appearance: background and workplane colours for the light theme, and the switch for edge lines on all bodies. The editor in the dark colour scheme. You set the colour scheme at the top right: System, Light, Dark or Graphite.

h: Appearance: axis arrows and edge lines
t: 「軸の矢印」 (on by default) draws three arrows at the back left corner of the plate: X in red to the right, Y in green to the back and Z in blue upwards, the way the position fields count. That is the right-hand rule Tinkercad, CAD programs and the slicers use too. With the workplane on a face they follow it. Switch them off here if they are in your way. 「すべてのボディにエッジ線」 draws an outline on every body, in the colour of 「エッジ線の色」 (black to begin with, as in Tinkercad): it helps when dark colours run into each other. It is off by default, and very large imported meshes are left out. Three dark bodies with edge lines switched on: the outlines keep them apart. 「穴をはっきり表示」 draws holes in a darker grey, less see-through and with a dark line round them. It helps when a hole is hard to find among see-through bodies. Unlike the edge lines it stays on in fast mode.

「影を表示」 switches the cast shadows on and off. Two sliders set how the bodies are lit. 「影の強さ」 says how dark the cast shadows are, and 「陰影のコントラスト」 moves light from the even ambient light to the main light: towards "punchy" the shaded sides get darker and the shadows show more, towards "soft" everything gets flatter. At the top end the contrast gets very strong, so shaded sides and shadows turn really dark. 「影の柔らかさ」 makes the edges of the shadows soft instead of crisp. 「光の方向」 turns the main light round the plate (0° from the front, 90° from the right), and 「光の高さ」 lifts it; at 90° it stands straight above the plate as in Tinkercad, and the shadows fall right under the bodies. 「やわらかい光」 brings most of the light from where you look, turning with the view: no face is left dark, and a face of a dark colour that points up is no longer burnt out to white. The main light stays a little for the shadows, and the contrast slider still works. If a bright reflection still shows with the light set low, lift 「光の高さ」 to 90°: it then looks like Tinkercad. 「光と影をリセット」 puts everything back.

「移動時の寸法を表示」 shows by how much you move while dragging or with the arrow keys, 「原点からの距離を表示」 the distances of the selection to the origin of the plate, also with several bodies selected. With 「寸法を常に表示」 these measures stay visible permanently, and not only while you drag. While a turned body is selected, its angles show below it on the workplane; 「回転したボディの角度を表示」 switches that off. More in Measuring and notes.

「移動の前に選択する」: a body then has to be selected first, and only the next drag moves it. That helps when children or hurried hands touch bodies, and on a touch screen. 「枠をドラッグする向きで決める」: a frame dragged to the right selects only what lies completely inside it, one dragged to the left everything it touches (drawn dashed), as in SketchUp. 「ダブルクリックでスケッチを開く」 decides whether a double click on an extruded sketch opens the sketch again, as in Tinkercad, and 「ダブルクリックでグループまたはバンドルを開く」 whether a double click on a group or a bundle opens it for editing. 「作業平面をダブルクリックするとそこがビューの中央になる」 decides whether a double click on empty workplane moves the view to that spot. 「移動中に他のシェイプにスナップ」 lets the edges and the centre of a shape snap to other shapes while you drag it; the grid menu at the bottom right has the same switch. 「新しいシェイプを追加するときにカメラを移動」 makes a new shape hang on the mouse pointer and land on the face under it, like Cruise in Tinkercad; switched off, a new shape appears in the middle of the plate. More in Selecting and arranging.

「エディターを透視投影表示で開始」: the editor then opens in the perspective view, not in the flat one. 「スクロールバーを表示してエディターを開始」: a design then opens with the view's scrollbars shown. It is saved with the design and with 「初期値にする」. 「開始ビュー」 sets the angle a new design opens in and 「ホームビュー」 goes back to. Turn and zoom the view the way you like it, then click 「現在のビューを使う」; 「標準」 brings back the usual view from the front right. It holds for every design in this browser. A design you open again still opens the way you left it. 「ズーム速度」 is a slider from slow to fast: how fast the wheel and the trackpad zoom; the zoom buttons and keys keep their own small steps. 「カメラの慣性」: after you let go of the mouse the view turns on for a moment and slows down gently. Switched off, it stops at once, as in Tinkercad and Fusion 360. 「{angle}°からオーバーハングを表示」 is the angle from which a face counts as an overhang when you switch on Show overhangs in the visibility menu: those faces are hatched red and white. 30° is careful, 70° counts on good cooling of the print; 45° is the usual start. While they are shown, a line under the view says the steepest overhang and how many cm² need supports. 「読み込んだメッシュの切り抜き上限」 limits how many triangles an imported mesh may have when you cut, merge or intersect it, because that is calculated in your browser. A mesh above the limit is not processed; simplify the mesh first, or raise the limit if your computer can take it. A higher limit can freeze the editor for a few seconds.

h: Measurement: units, scale and snap steps
t: Under 「計測」 you set the 「単位」, the unit that measures are shown in (「縮尺」: millimetres, centimetres or metres in metric, inches or feet in imperial), how many decimal places a number shows (「精度」), the 「スナップグリッド」 that moving and resizing snap to and your own snap steps under 「カスタムスナップグリッド」. Under 「計測」 in the settings you set the 「単位」. With 「ヤード・ポンド法」, layerling shows every measure in inches, on the shape, in the properties panel, on the tape measure and the ruler. The snap grid then offers steps from 1/64 to 1 inch, and the grid on the plate is drawn in inches (1/8 to 1 inch, 1/4 inch by default) with a stronger line on every whole inch. Under 「インチの表示」 you choose whether inches appear as fractions like in Tinkercad (1 5/8, rounded to 1/64 inch) or as decimals (1.625) with as many decimal places as set under 「精度」. You can type either, "1 5/8" included. A quick way between millimetres and inches is the small switch mm | in beside the 「スナップグリッド」 at the bottom of the properties window: it changes the unit, the plate's grid and the snap step as the settings do, for this design. Under 「カスタムスナップグリッド」 in the same place you add snap steps of your own: a name and a size in millimetres, for example "Pin pitch 2.54 mm" for the spacing of DIP chips, pin headers and perfboard holes, or "MX Key Unit" with 19.05 mm for the spacing of keyboard keys. The snap step menu then offers that measure whole, halved and quartered (1 ×, ½ × and ¼ ×), so shapes can be moved by one pitch, half a pitch or a quarter pitch. If you want just the measure itself, untick 「半分と4分の1も」 beside it; the menu then has only that one step. Custom steps are kept with the design and go along with 「初期値にする」. 「新しいデザインを原点に角定規を置いて開始」: every new design in this browser then starts with a framing square at the origin, see Measuring and notes. Designs you already have stay as they are, and a square you remove from a design stays removed.

「プリンター」 sizes the workplane to the build plate of your printer and flags bodies that reach past it, see Printing. 「プレートのラベル」 writes the design's name on the plate, and the printer's name and build volume when a printer is chosen. 「Printer play」 is the room per side a printed pin needs to turn in a printed hole on your printer. 「Make fit test」 puts the fit test that measures it on the plate, and new lids, dovetails, snap-fits, nuts and the clearance check then start from it, see Printing. It is kept in this browser, not in the design. 「作業平面のサイズ」 gives the plate a size of your own, with 「幅」 and 「長さ」 in millimetres or the unit you chose. The grid always runs through the origin, so the stronger lines lie on the axes whatever the plate measures.

「グリッドを表示」 shows or hides the grid on the plate. 「グリッドブロックのサイズ」 sets the spacing of its lines, and 「濃いグリッド線の間隔」 whether the darker line comes every 5 or every 10 grid steps; 「濃い線の色」 gives that line a colour of its own, and the centre cross and the plate border take it too. 「グリッドの色」 is the colour of the ordinary lines. Every line of the grid grows wider as you zoom in, as in Tinkercad, and stays visible as you zoom out. If that is too much for you, switch off 「ズームでグリッド線を太くする」 and the lines stay one pixel wide at every zoom, as in the sketch. If the grid has disappeared, say because a colour was set to that of the plate, 「グリッドをリセット」 at the end of the 「作業平面」 area brings its visibility, colours, spacing and line weight back to the standard, here and in the default saved with 「初期値にする」.

Under 「シェイプの初期値」 you choose a shape with 「シェイプ」 and set how it starts when you add it: its width, length and height. 「アプリの初期値を使う」 takes the shape back to what the app starts it with. Shapes with settings of their own show them under 「シェイプの詳細」. The values apply to new shapes, not to those already on the plate. 「カスタムサイズ上限」 sets a ceiling of your own for how large the handles and the properties may make that shape; left blank, the usual limits stay.

Under 「履歴」 the slider 「保存する履歴」 sets how many completed actions stay available for Undo after you save or reopen a design. The default is 100 actions in a design. A lower limit permanently discards the older undo steps of the design.

layerling calculates and draws everything in your browser. On an older computer, with a weak graphics card or on several large screens the view can therefore feel sluggish. This helps: 「高速モード」 under 「外観」 turns off at once everything that costs the view a lot: shadows, edge lines on all bodies and the camera's inertia. It also draws the view at the screen's own resolution only, which on high-resolution screens is up to four times fewer pixels. Your own settings are kept and apply again as soon as you turn it off. The camera keeps turning: When you let go of the mouse after turning, the view turns on for a moment and slows down gently. That is on purpose, not stutter. If you are used to Tinkercad or Fusion 360, turn off 「カメラの慣性」 under 「外観」, and the view stops at once. Single switches: Without fast mode you can also turn off just 「影を表示」 or 「すべてのボディにエッジ線」. Use the graphics card: In Chrome open chrome://gpu (in Edge edge://gpu). Next to "WebGL" it should say "Hardware accelerated". If it says "Software only", hardware acceleration is off in the browser's settings. On Windows you can also pick "High performance" for the browser under Settings → System → Display → Graphics, so it uses the real graphics card and not the weaker one in the processor. Simplify large imported meshes: A model of many hundred thousand triangles slows any view down. How to thin it out is in the chapter on files, under "Simplifying an imported mesh". Close other tabs: Every open layerling tab and every other 3D page shares the same graphics card.

The shape library, dimensions by number and by handle, colour, rotating, tapering and twisting. Every part in layerling starts with a shape. From them you build everything else: shapes complement each other, cut each other out or are joined into a new shape.

Click 「シェイプを追加」 in the ribbon. The shape library opens. The shape library. Every little picture is rendered from the shape's real geometry. The library is one list in sections, from 「Basic shapes」 to 「Helpers」, each with the number of shapes in it. A click on a section's name folds it away, and the browser keeps what you folded; the first time, all of them are open. On top, 「Recently used」 holds the last four shapes you put in. The search field finds a shape by its name and by other words for it, in English and German too: "USB" finds the 「ポート開口」. While you type, only the sections with a match show; an empty field brings your folded sections back as they were. 「カスタムシェイプ」 on top is a single line until you keep a shape there. The library closes after each shape you pick. Its title bar moves it, so you can put it where it does not cover the spot you are aiming at, over the properties panel for example; a double-click on the title bar puts it back under its button, and where you left it is kept in the browser. The pin in the title bar keeps the library open while you put several shapes one after the other. Its edges and corners pull its size, as wide and as high as your screen allows; the size is kept in the browser too, and a double-click on an edge sets it back. Pulled narrow, the library leaves out the names and shows only the pictures; the name appears when you point at a shape. Pick a shape. It now hangs on the mouse pointer and lands where you click. Move it over a body and it lies down on the face under the pointer, sloped ones too, like Cruise in Tinkercad; over the empty plate it lands on the workplane. Esc cancels placing. A tool that waits for a click, such as the tape measure, the framing square, a note, 「作業平面を配置」, 「面を下にして平らに置く」 or the edge tools, is switched off when you pick a shape, so the click places the shape. The other way round, switching one of those tools on puts the shape down again. If you would rather have the shape appear in the middle of the plate, you can switch off placing by click in the settings (area 「外観」, switch 「新しいシェイプを追加するときにカメラを移動」). On a face the shape snaps to the middle of that face when the pointer comes near it, as a corner or an edge snaps; hold Alt to set it down anywhere. Dragged from the library onto a face instead, it always lands in the middle of the face, or with Alt where you let go. What the library offers: 「Basic shapes」: 「直方体」, 「角丸直方体」, 「円柱」, 「カプセル」, 「楕円」, 「多角形」 (three to twenty-four sides), 「くさび」, 「球」, 「円錐」, 「曲面コーン」 (its side bends inward into a trumpet like a pseudosphere or outward into a dome; 「上面の直径」 and 「曲がり」 set it, and it can be hollowed out and filleted like any exact body), 「角錐」 (with three to twenty-four sides, so three-sided too), 「かまぼこ」, 「半球」, 「パラボラ」 (a dome that narrows to a rounded tip, its height falling with the square of the distance from the axis) and 「トーラス」. 「Vessels, tubes & transitions」: the 「ロフト」 from one outline to another, say from square to round, the 「パイプ」, the 「曲がりパイプ」, made of up to twelve straight pieces with bends in between, and the 「花びん」. 「Holes & cut-outs」: the 「座ぐり」 and 「皿穴」 for screw heads, the 「しずく型」 for horizontal holes and the 「ポート開口」 for USB, HDMI, DisplayPort and RJ45 sockets. 「Connections」: 「ねじ」 (threaded rod, screw, nut and tapped hole), the 「化粧座金」 under a countersunk screw, the print-in-place 「ヒンジ」 and the 「あり溝」. More in Threads and mechanics. 「Enclosure parts」: the 「Screw boss」 for heat-set inserts and self-tapping screws, the 「Snap-fit」 with its catch and the 「Rib」 or gusset. More in Threads and mechanics. 「Mechanics & moving parts」: 「ばね」, 「歯車」, the 「ハースカップリング」 and the 「GT2プーリー」. 「Systems & templates」: 「Gridfinity」 bins and baseplates, and the 「SBCボード」, a single-board computer true to size to build a case around. 「Lettering & signs」: 「テキスト」, also along a circular arc, the 「ネームタグ」, the 「アイコンタグ」 and the 「QRコード」. More in Text. 「Decorative outlines」: 「星」, 「ハート」, 「三日月」 and the 「ローレット」 for grips. 「Helpers」: the 「定規」, which is only a measuring tool and never shows up in an export. You get a triangle in two ways: the 「多角形」 with three sides is an isosceles triangle, the "Roof" of Tinkercad, and the 「くさび」 is a right triangle. Both are true triangular prisms. For a triangular hole, copy the shape, make the copy smaller, mark it as a hole and line it up with 「作業平面の中央に置く」 or 「整列」. Both work with the shape's bounding box, the smallest box that encloses it, so a halved square still counts as a whole square. The command search (Ctrl+K) also finds both shapes under "triangle" or "roof". The 「カプセル」 can be narrower at one end than at the other, say for a guard over a belt between two pulleys. Under 「プロパティ」 set 「小さい側の端（直径）」; the large end is as wide as the capsule, and the sides run straight from one arc to the other. 「中心距離」 is the distance between the two arcs' centres, that is how far apart the pulleys are. Change the small end and the centre distance stays, the capsule getting longer or shorter. The tapered capsule stays an exact body too, for fillets and STEP.

As soon as a shape is selected, its settings appear on the right. At the top is the name; the pencil beside it (「名前を変更」) lets you type a new one. Enter keeps it, Esc cancels, and an empty name brings back the shape's default name. Further right, the padlock locks the shape against accidental moving and the eye hides it. The arrow on the far left folds the settings down to their title bar. The cards below fold open and shut with a click on their title (「プロパティ」, 「位置」, 「回転」, 「テーパー」, 「ねじれと傾き」 and the cards of the special shapes); layerling remembers which ones you left open, for the next shape and the next visit. The settings sit docked at the right edge. If they cover something you want to see, drag them by their title bar and they float wherever you drop them; they stay there for the next shape too. Drop them back at the top right, or double-click the title bar, and they dock again. While they float or are folded down, the snap step moves from the bottom of the settings to the bottom right of the workplane. The settings of a cylinder: solid or hole, diameter and height as a number and as a slider. 「ソリッド」 or 「穴」: A solid stays, a hole takes material away. A click on 「ソリッド」 opens the colours; colours of your own that you mix there wait under 「最近使った色」 afterwards, the last eight. More in Solids and holes. The pin in the row 「とっておく色」 keeps the colour you have chosen for good: it stands in a row of its own, newer colours never push it out, and the same pin lets go of it again; up to 21 colours are kept in this browser. 「透明」: Lets you see through the body, for example to spot a shape behind it. 「マルチカラー」: For a group or a bundle; Shift+M switches it. Switched on, every part of the group shows in its own colour, also in a group that was cut with holes into one body (the walls a hole leaves take the colour of the body they were cut into). Picking a colour for the group switches it off and colours the whole group; the parts keep their own colours underneath, so switching it on again brings them back. A bundle has it switched on to begin with, and when it is switched off the bundle shows and exports in one colour. A group of solids only that you make starts with it switched off and shows as one body; groups made before keep showing their parts' colours. In a 3MF export every part keeps its colour, so the slicer can map the parts onto filaments; OBJ carries the colours on its points, so the border between two colours is a little rougher there. 「プロパティ」: The dimensions and everything that belongs to this shape. For a cylinder the diameter, the height and the number of sides. For a round tube or ring the 「外径」, the 「内径」 (for a bushing on a shaft of a known size) and the wall thickness: any two give the third, in whatever order you type them. The outer diameter keeps the bore and changes the wall, the inner diameter keeps the outer one and changes the wall, and a bore wider than the tube makes the outer diameter grow by the wall. The tube's length is its height. A tube that is not round, after you pulled one of its sides, has the sides Length and Width instead of the one outer diameter; there the wall stays when you change the width. For a gear the teeth, for a spring the turns. A value you have moved away from its default gets a small arrow next to its name: a click takes just that value back, whatever else you did since, unlike Undo. A double click on a slider does the same, here and for the sliders in the workspace settings. Dragged with the mouse, the slider of a length snaps to the snap step, so a height comes out in whole millimetres (not with the grid off, and not on short sliders); a typed value and the arrow keys on the slider stay exact. 「初期値として保存」 at the bottom makes the current values the start values of this kind of shape (the same as 「シェイプの初期値」 in the settings), and 「初期値をリセット」 goes back to the app's own. With 「グループ化するとき穴として切り抜く」 the bore counts as a hole once the tube is grouped: it then also cuts the wall of what the tube is grouped with, so two tubes in a T-junction open into each other. A bent tube with an opening has the same switch. 「楕円にする」: Only on a cylinder. A cylinder is always round: it has one diameter, and every handle changes both sides together. For an oval, click this and it becomes an 「楕円」 - the same body, whose length and width you then set one by one. A cylinder with a chamfer, a fillet or a wall, or a turned or grouped one, cannot be changed this way; take the 「楕円」 from the start for those. 「テーパー」: Different sizes at the top and bottom, for example for a slope or a funnel. With 「比率を保つ」 switched on, Length and Width of the same end change together in the ratio they have, so a square top stays square; top and bottom stay separate. 「ねじれと傾き」: Twists the top against the bottom or shifts it sideways. That gives twisted columns and leaning towers. 「長さ方向の勾配」: Runs the top down towards one end. 「低い側の端」 picks the end, 「端の高さ」 or 「勾配 (°)」 how low it goes, and 「カーブ (%)」 whether the top runs straight (0), bulges up (above 0) or sags (below 0). The other end keeps the body's height. Once it is set, an orange dot sits on the top of the lower end; drag it up and down like the height. That gives a roof whose height runs down along its length, a ramp or a slanted pipe end. 「長さ方向の絞り」: Seen from above, runs both long sides in evenly towards one end, so that end stays in the middle. 「細くなる端」 picks the end, 「端の幅」 its width (0 makes a point), 「開始位置 (%)」 where along the length the narrowing begins (0 % at the wide end, 50 % in the middle), and 「カーブ (%)」 whether the sides run straight (0), bulge out like a boat's bow (above 0) or are drawn in (below 0). Its orange dot sits on the side of the narrow end and moves across. Together with 「長さ方向の勾配」 it makes a bow or a ridge that runs down and in at once. A group of an orange block, a blue peg and a hole, cut into one body. With Multicolor switched on, the peg stays blue, the block orange, and the walls of the hole take the block's colour. Taper and twist work on almost every shape. Only the gear, thread, spring, Gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bent tube, teardrop, port opening, the screw-head cutters and the ruler leave them out: they have fixed measures of their own or, like the pyramid, a top of their own already. A cone whose top radius and height were changed: a small arrow next to each takes the value back, and the two buttons at the bottom save or reset the defaults of the shape. 「初期値として保存」 keeps what you changed on this shape as the start of every new shape of its kind: the sizes, the settings of the shape and its colour. Colour a cylinder green, press the button, and every cylinder you add from then on is green; the other kinds keep their own colours. 「初期値をリセット」 takes the kind back to what the app starts it with. The kinds that have defaults of their own are marked in the settings under 「シェイプの初期値」. A new design that you start from the start page begins with them too; the values are kept in this browser. A tapered or leaning box, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube or ring keeps its exact shape, and so do the capsule, star, heart, crescent, dovetail a rounded box without rounded top and bottom edges, and a straight or round knurl (its chamfered ends narrow with it): chamfers and fillets work on it as on the plain shape, and the STEP export writes it. The same holds for a twisted shape: its section turns exactly as it rises, and the sides wind evenly from bottom to top. 「長さ方向の勾配」 is offered on the box, rounded box, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube, ring, wedge and round roof. The wedge and the round roof lie along their depth, so they slope to the front or the back only. The sloped body keeps its exact shape, so chamfers, fillets and the STEP export work on it as on the plain shape; only a rounded box with rounded top and bottom edges, and a slope together with a taper, a twist or a lean, stay on the display mesh. 「長さ方向の絞り」 is offered on the same shapes except the tube and the ring, whose wall would get thinner across than along. A narrowed box, and a wedge or round roof narrowing, sloping or both, keep their exact shape in the same way. For now the display mesh only covers the rest: a narrowed cylinder, ellipse, polygon or rounded box, and a box that slopes and narrows at once. Chamfers, fillets and the STEP export then work on that mesh rather than on an exact body. Typing is more exact than dragging. All number fields take millimetres, but also percentages: type "50 %" into a width of 40 mm and you get 20 mm. They calculate too: "15*3", "120-2*4" or "(40+2)/2" give 45, 112 and 21; x works instead of *. The field remembers the calculation, in the properties panel as well as in the dimension boxes around the selected body: click into it again later and the formula stands there instead of the number, as long as the value still matches it, and you change it in place, "(140+2)/2" becoming "(40+6)/2". Drag the body by a handle or scale it and the formula no longer fits, so the field shows just the number again. In a number field you have clicked, the mouse wheel and the keys ↑ and ↓ change the value by one step, with Shift a larger step and with Alt a finer one. In a size or position field Shift steps by the snap grid instead, and by ten steps when the grid is off. It also works without clicking into a field: hold the mouse button down on the name of a value, say "Width", and drag left or right; the value changes as you drag, with the same keys as the wheel.

A click on 「ソリッド」 in the properties of a body opens the colour card, headed 「シェイプの色」. On top it shows the hex value of the colour the body has now. Under it are the ready colours of the palette; a click on one colours the body and closes the card. 「カスタム」 opens the colour picker of your browser, for a colour of your own. What it offers depends on the browser: in Chrome and Edge it has a colour field, a slider for the hue, an eyedropper that takes a colour from anywhere on the screen, and the value as HEX, RGB or HSL, which you switch with the arrows beside it. The colour counts when you close the picker or click outside it. A colour of your own that you mix there waits under 「最近使った色」 afterwards, the last eight. The pin in the row 「とっておく色」 keeps the colour you have chosen for good: it stands in a row of its own, newer colours never push it out, and the same pin lets go of it again; up to 21 colours are kept in this browser. The pin is for colours of your own, the ones of the palette are always there. With several colours selected, or with a hole, there is no single colour to keep. The colours of the work area in the settings have a simpler picker of their own, with a colour field, a row of ready colours and a field for the hex value; see The settings.

h: How round is round? The side count
t: Round shapes such as cylinder, cone, tube, ellipse or the bores have the switch 「辺の数をサイズに合わせる」 and the slider 「辺の数」 in their properties. The 「トーラス」 has two sliders: 「リングの分割数」 around the ring and 「チューブの分割数」 around the tube. They follow the size there too until you hold them, so a large torus shows no facets. The reason: for the view and for STL, 3MF and OBJ, layerling draws a circle as a polygon of many small sides. The more sides, the smoother it is, and the more triangles it takes. The 「チューブの太さ」 sets how thick the tube is seen from above. The height only squashes or stretches the tube, so a flat ring keeps its hole; at half the outer size the hole closes. Dragging the handles scales the tube along. Only a torus whose tube is as thick as the torus is high stays an exact body for chamfers, fillets and STEP. Where the side count matters In the export for the slicer (STL, 3MF, OBJ). A cylinder with few sides arrives there as a polygon. When bodies and holes are combined. A bore cut by a hole with few sides is angular in the finished part. That includes screw holes. In the view. Many very fine shapes slow the editor down. Where it does not matter For the STEP export. It writes the round shape, not the polygon. For chamfers and fillets (「面取り」, 「フィレット」) as long as the shape stays round. That is the case when you have not set a side count, when the count is at least the shape's default, or when the polygon strays at most 0.05 mm from the circle. The default is 96 sides for cylinder, ellipse, tube and cone, 64 for the 「かまぼこ」, 24 steps for the 「球」, 32 for the 「半球」 and the 「パラボラ」, 96 sides and 24 steps for the 「トーラス」, and a 「品質」 of 32 for a round 「曲がりパイプ」. For a thread, a spring or a helical or herringbone gear. The edge tool and the STEP export take its exact body; its 「品質」 only sets how finely it is drawn. Where it matters again For chamfers and fillets on a shape with few sides. If you set the side count below the default, the edge tool takes the shape as it is drawn: a cylinder with 6 sides stays a hexagonal bar, and the fillet runs round its six edges. That is how you can build, for instance, a nut pocket with rounded corners. For a round shape, leave 「辺の数をサイズに合わせる」 on. How to use it Leave 「辺の数をサイズに合わせる」 on. Then layerling picks the side count from the diameter so that the polygon strays at most 0.005 mm from the true circle, far below what a printer resolves. Small shapes get at least 24 sides, large ones more. Fewer sides you take when you want a polygon on purpose (but there is the 「多角形」 for that) or when the editor gets slow with very many round shapes. More sides you hardly ever need. Only on very large round parts, when you see edges in the STL. For parts you only treat with edges or hand on as STEP, the side count does not matter.

Besides the settings there are handles on the shape itself: The corners and edges make the shape larger or smaller. Drag one past the opposite side and the shape keeps growing there, on the other side of that edge. The arrow on top does the same below the base. Hold Shift while dragging a corner to scale width, depth and height together and keep the proportions; hold Alt to scale from the center instead of the opposite corner. Without a keyboard, or if you do not want to hold a key, switch on 「比率を保つ」 at the top of the properties: then the corners always keep the proportions, and typing one of width, depth or height scales the other two by the same factor. The setting is remembered. The black arrow above the shape lifts or lowers it; with Alt held from the start, a copy is made where you let go, so you can stack. The handle on the top face changes the height. The handles that change one measure carry the colour of its axis, as the curved arrows do: the middle of a side (width red, depth green) and the top (height blue); the corners change two measures and stay white. The red and the green arrows on top move the shape along X or along Y only. The shape then follows the mouse along that line, even when you look at the plate from low down, where a free drag runs off far. It snaps to other shapes as a drag does, and afterwards you can click the distance moved and type the exact value. The curved arrows rotate it. The numbers beside the shape show the dimensions. A click on one opens a field in which you type the number you want. With Enter the shape grows from the edge opposite the number, as when you drag; with Alt+Enter it grows round its middle, so a shape that was aligned with another stays aligned. With 「比率を保つ」 ticked in the properties, or with Shift+Enter, the other two dimensions follow by the same factor. That holds for width and length; the height always grows upward from the underside. The fields in the properties on the right keep the middle without a key. Tab keeps the number and opens the next one (width, depth, height); Shift+Tab goes back. In a field of the properties that you have clicked, the mouse wheel changes the value as well: a unit a notch, ten times as much with Shift (in a size or position field the snap grid), a tenth with Ctrl and a hundredth with Alt. A field that you have not clicked leaves the wheel to the panel, which scrolls. A click on a corner (without dragging) opens width and depth together. Type the first, press Tab for the second and Enter to apply both. Esc cancels. Once a shape is turned by right angles, for instance laid on its side with 「面を下にして平らに置く」, the fields in the properties are named after the direction each measure runs in now: 「高さ」 is what goes up, 「幅」 runs along X and 「長さ」 along Y. Typing the height of a shape lying down therefore changes the vertical measure, and its underside stays on the plate. A shape tilted at any other angle shows its own measures in the fields, and a note below says so. Without the mouse, use the keyboard: the arrow keys move the selection by one snap step (0.01 mm when the grid is off), with Shift by five, or by ten if you set 「濃いグリッド線の間隔」 to 「10グリッド刻み」 in the settings under 「外観」: as far as the next darker line, as in Tinkercad. They follow the view: → moves to where the screen's right is, ↑ away from you, even after turning the plate. Push a shape out of the picture and the view moves along. Ctrl+↑ and Ctrl+↓ raise and lower it. A run of arrow presses is one step in the history: as long as the next press follows within a second and a half, Undo takes back the whole run, not a press at a time. R rotates by 45°, Shift+R by 22.5°. D drops the selection onto the workplane. The handles pull a shape as large as your plate, at least 220 mm wide and deep. Typing a number in the properties goes beyond that, and a shape made that large does not shrink back when you grab it again. A ceiling of your own per shape is set in the settings under 「シェイプの初期値」 with 「カスタムサイズ上限」. The snap step is at the bottom right of the editor and can be changed at any time.

「コピー」, 「貼り付け」 and 「複製」 are in the ribbon (「クリップボード」). Ctrl+D duplicates a selection. layerling remembers how you last moved or rotated the copy and applies the same again on the next duplicate. That produces a row of holes or steps in a few key presses. For regular arrangements there is also the pattern, described in Selecting and arranging. If you also resized the copy, every further copy grows by the same factor again, as in Tinkercad. A shape you gave a name of your own gets a copy that is called after it, "Holder (copy)", then "Holder (copy 2)" and so on, so the object list stays readable; a shape that only has the name layerling handed out ("Box") keeps it. Tip: If a shape refuses to take the size you want, it is often the limits for new shapes. Under 「シェイプの初期値」 in the settings you decide how each shape starts and how large it may get.

A holder, a grip or a base plate you need again and again goes into the 「カスタムシェイプ」. They sit at the top of the shape library, above the 「基本シェイプ」, and fold away with their arrow. Select one or more bodies, holes, groups or an imported model included. Open the shape library and click 「選択を保存」. Enter a name and confirm with 「保存」. In any design, a click on the tile inserts the shape, like any other shape. You can also drag the tile onto the workplane; it then lands where you let go. The shape then hangs on the pointer, like any other: it follows it, also over the faces of other bodies, and a click sets it down; Esc puts it away. Several bodies come back together, placed as they stood to each other, and stay selectable one by one. Notes pinned to the saved bodies go along and come back closed, pinned to the inserted ones; free notes and reference points stay in the design. The pencil on a tile renames it, the bin removes it after asking. Shapes already inserted into designs stay as they are. The 「カスタムシェイプ」 live in this browser, apart from the designs, and are there again the next time you start. 「すべてバックアップ」 on the start page backs them up with the designs, and opening the backup brings both back. To take only the shapes to another browser, 「カスタムシェイプをバックアップ」 (the arrow pointing down) saves them as a ZIP file and 「シェイプを読み込む」 (the arrow pointing up) brings them back there. 「シェイプを読み込む」 also takes single .lyl designs; each one becomes a shape. Shapes already there are not added twice.

Many custom shapes sort better into folders. 「新しいフォルダー」 (the folder with the plus, next to 「選択を保存」) asks for a name and makes a folder at the top; the folder with the plus on a folder, 「この中に新しいフォルダー」, makes one inside it. Folders go three levels deep: a folder on the third level holds shapes but no further folders. Folders sit above the shapes that are in none, in the order of their names, and open and close with their arrow; the number on a folder counts the shapes in it and in the folders inside it. When saving, choose the folder in the list next to the name; 「フォルダーなし」 keeps the shape at the top. The folder with the arrow on a tile moves that shape into another folder, or back out with 「フォルダーなし」. The pencil on a folder renames it, the bin deletes it after asking, together with the folders and shapes in it. A folder itself cannot be moved: make the new one where it belongs and move the shapes over. A backup keeps the folders, and loading it puts the shapes back in the same place.

With the shared server store switched on, the section shows two groups: 「サーバー上」 and 「このブラウザー内」. When saving you choose where the shape goes; the server is chosen to start with. There it lives in the folder Custom shapes, as a .lyl file of its own with a picture, ready on every device that reaches the server; its folders are folders inside Custom shapes. Each side has folders of its own, and a shape moves between the folders of its side. The cloud on a browser tile puts that shape on the server; it is then no longer kept twice. The Custom shapes folder shows on the start page as well. Open a shape there like a design, change it, and it is saved automatically like any design on the server; the next insert takes the new version. As the server store has no login, everyone who reaches the server sees the same shapes.

Should a pattern, a logo or lettering go onto a cup, a can or a tube? First lay it flat on the plate, as an imported SVG or as text for example, the way it should look from above. Then wrap it around a cylinder in the shape's settings under 「円柱に巻き付ける」: Open 「円柱に巻き付ける」 and enter the 「直径」 of the cylinder wall, such as the outside diameter of your cup. Tenths of a millimetre work too, such as 63.5. Click 「巻き付ける」. What ran from left to right now runs around the cylinder, the back edge becomes the top, and the thickness stands out of the wall. Select the wrapped shape and the cylinder and centre both, left to right and front to back. The middle of the wrapped shape is the cylinder's axis, so it then sits right on its wall. Every body can be wrapped, a shape from the library too: a round roof, say, that should sit on the wall of a round tower. Lay it on the plate the way it should look on the wall, its round top at the back. For an engraving, switch on 「内側へ（彫刻）」: the thickness then goes into the wall. Make the shape a hole, centre it and group it with the cylinder. A shape that is wrapped already is a mesh of the wrapped thing and cannot be wrapped again: undo the wrapping, or wrap the flat original once more with another diameter. The result is a mesh like an imported model. Undo lays the shape flat again; for another diameter, undo first and wrap again. It cannot go further than once around the cylinder; then layerling names the smallest diameter that fits.

Grooves, knurling, honeycomb or bumps on a body, for a better grip or for looks: open 「表面テクスチャ」 in the shape's settings. The button 「表面テクスチャ」 in the 「変形」 group at the top does the same: it opens and closes the card for the selected body and stays lit while the card is open. Choose the 「模様」, its 「間かく」 and its 「深さ」. 「向き」 says whether it goes into the body or stands out of it. For 「つぶ」, 「つぶの形」 chooses between 「半球」, 「円すい（とがった）」, 「やわらかく丸い」 and 「上が平ら」. Under 「ならべ方」 they sit 「ずらしてならべる」, every other row half a spacing along, or in 「まっすぐならべる」. Under 「付け方」, take 「軸のまわり」 for round bodies such as a cup, a knob or a handle. The pattern runs round the 「軸」, and the spacing is rounded a little so that a whole number of grooves or cells goes round: the pattern closes without a seam. 「全体」 suits bodies that are not round, 「平ら、軸にそって」 a lid or a plate seen from above. Leave it at 「自動」 and Layerling chooses for you: 「軸のまわり」 on round bodies and on angular ones standing upright such as a box - the pattern then follows the outline and runs round the edges without a seam, a pattern standing out bending round them -, 「全体」 on other angular ones. Click 「テクスチャを適用」. A large body takes a few seconds; you can keep working meanwhile. To give the pattern to only some faces, say only the top of a box, click 「面を選ぶ」 and then the faces in the view: the top, the bottom or a side. A face reaches up to the body's sharp edges; on a cylinder the mantle is one face, and the top and the bottom are one each. Picked faces light up, a second click takes one out again, and 「すべての面にもどす」 gives the pattern the whole body again. Only the picked faces get the pattern; all others stay as they were and keep few triangles. On a top or a bottom the pattern lies flat; on a round top, grooves, rope and knitting run in rings round the middle, like a tree's year rings. 「上と下での向き（°）」 turns the pattern on the top and bottom: at 0° the rows run along the front edge, at 90° along the side edge. 「上と下」 switches grooves, rope and knitting there between rows and rings; on an angular body the rings follow its outline. 「上と下のエッジ」 says what happens at the edge between the side and a patterned top or bottom: 「かど」 lets both end at the edge. With 「側面がまわりこむ」 the side's pattern bends round the edge and takes the whole top: rows of rope, knitting and level grooves run on as rings, upright and slanted grooves as rays almost to the middle. 「少しだけ折り返す」 does the same as a rim only; inside lies the top's own pattern, as 「上と下」 sets it. 「ふちどり」 lays a border round the edge for every pattern – a cord, a cast-off chain or a round bead. A tight round (a fillet) ends a face as well: on a cup with rounded rims the outside, the rounds, the rim, the inside and the bottom are faces of their own, so a click on the outside takes only the outside. A wide round, about a quarter of the body or more, belongs to the face, as a sphere is one face. With picked faces, 「外側の壁」 and 「内側の壁」 do not count. Several patterns on one body – bricks round the sides, knurling on the top – are layers: 「Layer」 beside the first adds one, and picking is switched on for it at once; click the faces it should get. Every further layer goes only on its own faces, the first on all the others. The tabs show one layer at a time with its settings, 「Remove this layer」 takes one away. All layers are made together on the body under the texture, so changing one or taking the texture off works as for a single pattern. A text needs no faces as a layer: it goes where it is put. Under 「詳細」 you choose where the pattern goes: outer and inner walls, how far the bottom and the top stay smooth (a smooth bottom keeps the body flat on the bed), a band of the height, and whether sharp edges stay smooth. Next to everything that stays smooth, the pattern fades in gently; 「だんだん消える長さ」 sets over how many millimetres. The smaller it is, the closer the pattern comes to an edge; a pattern standing out runs out right up to it. On the flat sides of an angular body like a cube it ends at a straight border that far away instead: grooves and diamonds stop with a short wall, and only whole bumps stay. 「断面の形」 shapes the cross-section of a groove or joint: pointed and flat come out exactly, round in as many steps as 「細かさ」 gives it. Besides 「みぞ」, 「ローレット」, 「ハニカム」 and 「つぶ」 there are more patterns. 「セル」 are irregular cells like paving stones or dried clay; their joints are cut cleanly as the honeycomb's are, and another 「ならび方」 lays them out anew. 「編み目」, 「ロープ」 and 「かご編み」 copy knitted stitches, a wound rope and a basket of stakes and weavers; they start raised and round, at the size of their models. 「つぶつぶ」 roughens the surface finely, as if blasted; the grain lies in space, without a seam or stretching. 「画像」 takes a grey picture as a height map: one of the ready ones such as wood, topography or terrazzo, or your own with 「自分の画像を読みこむ…」. Light becomes the full depth; 「タイルの幅」 sets how wide a tile is, and under 「タイル」 the tiles repeat, mirror or are staggered. A dark drawing on a transparent ground, such as black lines in an SVG, counts by its lines: they become the full depth. With 「Once」 the image is pressed on a single time, like a label: 「まわりの角度（°）」 and 「高さ（%）」 place its middle as for a text, 「Image width」 sets its width, and the surface beside it stays smooth. With faces picked, it always lands on them, even where 「まわりの角度（°）」 and 「高さ（%）」 aim past them. 「カーボン（綾織り）」 lays carbon fibre woven in twill onto the body: upright bands and crossing bands, over and under each other, one band on from band to band, so the familiar diagonal shows. 「織り方」 chooses 「綾織り 2/2」, the even weave of most carbon parts, or 「綾織り 2/1」 and 「綾織り 3/1」, where the upright bands show long and the crossing ones short. 「帯の幅」 sets how wide the upright bands are; 「交わる帯の幅」 makes the crossing ones wider or narrower for an uneven weave (0: as wide). Round a body the band width is rounded a little so the weave closes without a seam. The single fibres are far too fine for a print: the bands with their crossings are what shows. 「レンガ」 lay a brick wall onto the body, with joints sunk in like mortar. 「積み方」 chooses how the bricks are laid: 「長手積み」 as most walls are, 「いも目地」, or with short bricks between the long ones (「イギリス積み」, 「オランダ積み」, 「フランス積み」). 「レンガの長さ」 and 「1段の高さ」 count from joint to joint and are rounded a little so that whole bricks fit: round a cup, from edge to edge of a box's side and from the bottom to the top; 「目地の幅」 says how wide the joints are. Under 「詳細」, 「レンガのふぞろいさ（%）」 lets every brick lie a little deeper, as in an old wall. 「Squares」 and 「Triangles」 lay tiles of one size in a grid onto the body, raised or pressed in, their walls cut steep and clean; the triangles stand in rows, pointing up and down in turn. 「Square size」 or 「Triangle size」 and 「Gap」 stay exactly as you set them – squares of 3.2 mm, 3.2 mm apart, are eight lines of a 0.4 mm nozzle each and print cleanly. The grid is centred on every face; round a round body the gap is rounded a little so that a whole number goes round. With 「From the bottom edge」 the first row starts right at the bottom edge and reaches down into the first layer, where a brim holds it. For tiles on only the lower half of two sides, pick the two faces and put a helper body over the upper half with 「テクスチャを付けない」 under 「テクスチャのマスク」 (see below).
