How an AI assistant such as Gemini, Claude or Codex creates and changes shapes, groups them and takes pictures of the view in your open editor. layerling comes with an MCP server. MCP is a standard through which an AI assistant can use tools in other programs. With it an AI client such as Gemini, Claude or Codex sees an open editor tab and works in it: it creates shapes, changes dimensions, groups, cuts, rounds edges, reads out the scene and takes pictures of the view. You describe the part, the AI builds it, you watch and can step in at any moment. The bridge between AI client and editor runs locally on your computer. Keep in mind, though: what the AI reads, meaning the scene and the pictures of the view, goes to the provider of your AI client, like any other input there. Important: The MCP bridge exists in the development server that you start yourself on your computer. On layerling.com and in installations with static hosting it is switched off. A copy you host yourself, such as the Docker image on a NAS, can switch it on with an access token; see "A copy on a NAS or server" below.

You do not need to know anything about programming for this. The shortest way: give your favourite AI the address of the project, https://github.com/henmedia/layerling, and ask it: "Set up layerling on my computer so that I can build 3D models with you through its MCP server." It downloads and installs everything itself and tells you when it is done. This works with an AI that can work on your computer, such as the Code tab of the Claude app, Codex, Antigravity or Gemini CLI. A chat in the browser cannot do it, because it cannot install anything on your computer. Or do it yourself, on Windows with the Claude app, in five steps: 1. Install layerling. Open the Start menu, type PowerShell and open Windows PowerShell. Copy this line, paste it into the window with a right-click and press Enter: irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/windows-quickstart.ps1 | iex It installs what layerling needs, downloads layerling into the folder layerling in your user folder (C:\Users\<your name>\layerling) and opens it in your browser. The first time this takes a few minutes. Windows PowerShell with the line pasted in. Press Enter, and it starts. 2. Keep layerling running. layerling runs as long as the PowerShell window stays open, and the AI can only build while it runs. Next time, double-click "Start layerling" on your desktop instead. 3. Install the Claude app. Install the Claude app for Windows and sign in. The Code tab used in the next step is part of the paid Claude plans. 4. Open the layerling folder in the Code tab. In the Claude app, switch to Code at the top and choose the folder layerling in your user folder as the folder to work in. layerling already brings everything Claude needs to find its tools. If Claude asks whether it may use the MCP server "layerling" of this folder, allow it. 5. Tell Claude what to build. For example: "Use the layerling tools and build me a round box, 60 mm across and 40 mm high, with a 2.5 mm wall." If no editor is open, Claude opens one in your browser, builds the box there step by step and takes pictures to check its work. You watch and can change anything yourself at any time. On a Mac it goes the same way, with these changes. In step 1, open the Terminal app (press Cmd+Space, type Terminal and press Enter), paste this line and press Enter: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/mac-quickstart.sh | sh If Git or Node.js is missing, it tells you what to install (macOS offers Git in a window, Node.js comes as an installer from nodejs.org); afterwards run the same line again. In step 2, the shortcut on your desktop is also called "Start layerling". In step 3, install the Claude app for Mac. Tip: If something does not work, tell Claude what you see. It can read the error and usually fixes it itself. If nothing happens in the editor, check first that layerling is still running (step 2).

Get layerling from GitHub and start it in the project folder with npm run dev. Node.js must be installed. On Windows the quick-start line in the README takes care of that. Open an editor tab, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000/?editor=1. You can leave that to the AI: when no editor is open, the first tool that needs one starts your browser with an editor and waits until it has connected. That works for a layerling on your own computer; a copy on a NAS or server needs you to open the editor. Set LAYERLING_MCP_OPEN_EDITOR=0 for the MCP server to switch it off. Connect your AI client to the MCP server. The client starts it itself with node scripts/layerling-mcp-server.mjs.

Nothing to install: the project brings a .mcp.json that registers the server, and the skill under .claude/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. Open the layerling folder in Claude Code and ask, for example: "Use the layerling MCP tools to list my open editors and inspect the scene."

Claude Desktop does not read project files. Enter the server in its own configuration. As a template use docs/mcp/claude-desktop-config.example.json in the project, replacing the script path with the absolute path on your computer. Then restart Claude Desktop.
Copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your Codex skills folder, enter the server in your Codex configuration using docs/mcp/codex-config.example.toml, and restart Codex.

Antigravity auto-discovers the workspace skill in .agents/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. For Gemini CLI, copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your global skills folder (~/.gemini/skills/), add the server to your settings using docs/mcp/gemini-config.example.json, and restart the client. The detailed instructions for each client are in the README on GitHub.

h: A copy on a NAS or server
t: A copy you host yourself can let an AI client drive its open editors over the network. It is off by default, because whoever can drive the bridge can read and change the open designs. On the server, set LAYERLING_MCP_REMOTE to true and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN to a secret of at least 16 characters (for the Docker image in environment: of the compose file; no rebuild needed). Open an editor tab of that copy and keep it open, and give the MCP client the address and the same token: LAYERLING_URL=http://nas:3000 and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN=<the token>. Only a client with the token can list or drive the editors. The editor pages need none, but they only count under an address or name that only your own network can use (an IP address, a name without a dot, or one ending in .local or .lan); a real domain behind a reverse proxy goes into LAYERLING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Use it on a network you trust, and HTTPS beyond it. The README has the details.

The AI works with the same functions as you, through the same path as your operation in the editor. New layerling functions get their MCP action right away. The tools: Tool What it does layerling_list_editors lists the open editor tabs layerling_rename_project gives the project a name, as the pencil beside the project name does layerling_open_editor opens a new editor tab in your default browser and waits until it has connected (on your own computer only) layerling_read_scene reads scene, selection, units and the exact dimensions of all objects layerling_list_objects lists all objects with dimensions, position, rotation and id layerling_select_objects selects objects layerling_hide_others hides everything but the selection or the given objects, in one undo step layerling_delete_objects deletes objects layerling_move_object moves an object to another place in the object list layerling_create_shape creates a shape: box, cylinder, text (also curved), thread, gear, sketch body and all the others layerling_import_file imports a file as the import window does, a coloured OBJ or 3MF as one body per colour, a 3MF with several objects as one body per object layerling_add_font adds a font of one's own for text from a TrueType, OpenType or WOFF file; it stays in the browser, a design keeps only the letters it uses layerling_list_fonts solid or hole and everything else that makes up the shape, a text's letter edge included layerling_align_objects aligns objects with each other layerling_scale_objects scales objects by a percentage, together or each in place layerling_lay_flat lays an object with one face on the plate layerling_place_on_face sets objects down on a face of another, sloped ones too, like the C key wraps the objects in one convex body, as if shrink-wrapped (Hull) layerling_cookie_cutter makes a cookie cutter from the objects: a wall with a cutting edge and a rim round the mirrored outline itself with gentle bends (Cable channel) layerling_loft_sketches joins two sketch bodies into a loft from one outline to the other (Loft sketches) layerling_separate_parts separates a shape into its loose parts, a sketch body into one body per outline layerling_split_objects cuts solids or holes in two with a plane layerling_list_edges lists the real CAD edges of an object layerling_apply_edge_treatment chamfers or fillets chosen edges layerling_hollow_object hollows a body with an even wall layerling_cut_out cuts one solid out of another so they fit: the part stays, a copy grown by the clearance is subtracted from the other body layerling_punch punches the outline of one solid, seen along x, y or z, straight through another; the punch stays and need not touch it layerling_offset_object builds the clearance of a press fit: grows or shrinks a solid, or adds the grown copy as a hole, or moves only the sides layerling_list_faces lists the faces of an exact body layerling_delete_faces deletes faces and closes the gap layerling_array_objects multiplies in a row, in a grid or on a circle layerling_bundle_objects bundles objects like Ctrl+B: they move together, stack again, with a key ring hole, the corners per layer and a rounded or chamfered letter edge; with a name list, one tag per name layerling_text_block makes a text block: a text becomes the first of several lines, each a text of its own under the one above, aligned left, centred or right, each line the same size or smaller layerling_layer_icon turns an SVG icon (the text of the file, or an extruded sketch body) into a layered icon tag for a multicolour print - the icon, wider rims, a plate without holes - or builds one again with a new width or layers; with a count it fills the plate with copies layerling_create_qr_code makes a QR code from a text or web address, like 「QRコード」 in the shape library - the code alone, raised on a plate or engraved, with error correction, width, 3 B+, Zero 2 W or BIGTREETECH Pi, with its holes and connectors, the clearance round the edge connectors, the position and as a hole to cut a case layerling_reference_image adds a reference image from measures it layerling_check_print checks before printing what would go wrong: walls too thin for the nozzle, floating parts, small contact with the plate, overhangs and open meshes (Print check) layerling_add_reference_points marks reference points - on the centre, corners or edge middles of objects, or at exact positions - that shapes snap to layerling_list_reference_points lists the each is pinned to and whether it is a request for the AI layerling_wait_for_notes waits until you tick 「For the AI」 on a note, and hands the request over at once layerling_add_note puts a note on the model, pinned to an object or free on the plate layerling_update_note changes a note or answers it; an answer closes the request layerling_remove_notes deletes notes by id layerling_inspect_errors shows the last message and the last error, plus the messages and errors of the session layerling_wrap_around_cylinder wraps a body lying flat, an SVG or text for example, around a cylinder, outward or inward as an engraving layerling_texture_surface lays a surface texture onto a body: grooves, knurling, honeycomb or bumps, for grip or for looks, and changes or removes it later cylinders, cones, spheres and tori become real faces, so edges round cleanly and STEP carries them layerling_save_custom_shape keeps bodies as a custom shape, on the server or in the browser, to insert them into other designs layerling_list_custom_shapes lists the custom shapes on the server and in the browser layerling_insert_custom_shape inserts a custom shape into the open design, at a spot x/z if you like layerling_delete_custom_shape removes a custom shape; inserted bodies stay layerling_show_workplane hides and shows the plate with its grid, for a picture of the underside for example (only the view) layerling_set_section_view cuts the view open along a plane to look inside (only the view, nothing is cut apart) layerling_measurements shows or hides the measurements of the tape measure and lists them with their lengths, hides or shows the sizes around the selection like Q, and types a length for one of them, which moves the body at its end like a click on its number layerling_measure_angle measures an angle like the protractor: at the corner of three points or between two flat faces, and shows it in the view layerling_saved_view saves the current view under the key 7, 8, 9 or 0 and goes back to it, like Shift+key and the key (only the view); also sets the start view of new designs layerling_build_plates lists, adds, names, orders and removes the build plates, moves objects onto a plate and arranges them on the plates, like the plate bar layerling_clear_history deletes every undo step for good, as the History view's "Delete history" button does; needs confirm: true layerling_set_history_view looks back at an earlier state of the project, like the History view (the real design stays untouched; changing tools wait until it is closed) layerling_restore_from_history brings objects (also parts inside groups) back from an earlier state into the design as copies, as the History view's Bring into design does - one step that undo takes back layerling_export_section_svg returns the outlines on a cutting plane as an SVG at 1:1, from the same bodies as the export layerling_sketch_from_section makes a sketch from the outlines on a cutting plane, lying on the cut: opened in the editor to change, or built at once into a body of a given height layerling_export_drawing makes the workshop drawing of the "2D" export: three views at 1:1 on an ISO sheet with overall sizes and a table of the round bores, as SVG text or PDF layerling_export_mesh writes the file of the export window as STL, 3MF, OBJ, SVG (top view, footprint or visible edges) or DXF for laser cutting, from the same bodies; to a path on this computer, or as base64 layerling_save_project saves the whole editable design as a .lyl file at a path on the computer where the MCP server runs, without a dialog; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite, it is written through a temporary file, and the target of Ctrl+S in the editor stays as it is layerling_list_attachments lists the files attached to the design (name, type, size), as the Attachments panel shows them layerling_get_attachment reads one attached file, its bytes as base64, as Download in the panel does layerling_add_attachment attaches a file given as base64, with the panel's checks; a name already attached is only overwritten with replace layerling_rename_attachment gives an attached file another name; its content stays layerling_remove_attachment removes an attached file for good; needs confirm: true layerling_set_workplane puts the workplane on a side of a body or back on the base plate, and hides or shows it layerling_capture_image takes a picture of the view: front, top, side, diagonally from a corner and more That lets the AI check itself: it creates something, takes a picture, looks and improves.

You say: "Build me a round box 60 mm across, 40 mm high with a 2.5 mm wall, open at the top, plus a flat lid with 'Tea' written in an arc." The AI creates the cylinders, hollows one, puts the curved text on the lid and takes pictures at the end to see whether it fits. Tip: Give the AI concrete dimensions and tell it what the part is for ("holder for a 12 mm rod, fits a Bambu Lab A1"). Then it makes more sensible decisions. And watch it build: you can step in yourself at any time, because it is the same editor.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: Start layerling like a normal program, even without a network, and how to run it on your own computer.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: layerling can be installed like a normal program. It then gets an icon and a window of its own, without an address bar. After the first visit it starts even without internet. Your designs stay on your computer. Installing is worth it: the app starts faster, because it does not have to be loaded again each time, it works without internet and it spares the server. You lose nothing, as layerling still tells you when a new version is out. This also protects your designs: Safari on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad clears the stored data of a website that has not been visited for seven days, but not that of an installed app. On the start page a hint with 「今すぐインストール」 appears if your browser can do it. Otherwise: Chrome and Edge: Click the install icon at the right of the address bar, or choose "Install as app" in the browser menu. Safari on the Mac: Menu "File", then "Add to Dock". Safari on iPhone and iPad: Share icon, then "Add to Home Screen". Firefox: cannot install apps. layerling still starts offline in a tab there. You can close the hint on the start page with 「このヒントを非表示」. Starting the installed app a second time in Chrome or Edge brings the open window to the front instead of opening another one. On a computer, an installed layerling in Chrome or Edge also registers as a program for .lyl files: a double click on a design in the file manager opens it in layerling, and Ctrl+S saves back into that file. It does the same for .stl and .3mf files, which open as a new design, as with 「デザインを開く、またはジオメトリを読み込む」 on the start page. To make layerling the default for them, choose it under Open with and let the system always use it. On Android this does not work, there the browser offers no file association for installed web apps; open a design with 「デザインを開く、またはジオメトリを読み込む」 on the start page.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: When a newer version exists, layerling shows it on the start page. Through 「リリースノートとダウンロード」 you read what has changed. The version number is at the bottom right. After reloading the page you have the new version. On layerling.com and on other web servers an open page notices an update by itself. It asks the server for its version now and then, when you come back to the tab, and at once if a program file it needs has disappeared. When something new was installed in the meantime, a card at the bottom right says so and lists what is new. 「保存して再読み込み」 writes the design you have open into the browser first and then loads the page again; the design comes back as you left it. 「後で」 holds the card back for 15 minutes. Reload soon: a page that stays on the old version may load parts of the new one that do not fit. The same card appears when that has already happened: the CAD workers, which load only when you first need them, say which build they are from, and if it is not the page's own - after an update, or with a stored copy of an older version - the card asks for a reload before the two misunderstand each other. When layerling is open in several tabs, they look out for each other: if another tab already runs a newer version, a note at the bottom of the old tab asks you to reload it. And if the same design is open in two tabs, both warn you, because they save automatically and would overwrite each other. If you open layerling in one more tab while one is already open, the new tab suggests carrying on in the old one and offers to close itself. If you want two tabs on purpose, say for two designs side by side, click 「ここで作業を続ける」 there. This guide opens in a tab of its own as well: while layerling is open next to it, its button at the top right reads "Back to the editor" and closes the guide instead of opening the editor a second time.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: You choose the language at the top right, from the language list. The colour scheme beside it offers 「システム」 (follows the operating system), 「ライト」, 「ダーク」 and 「グラファイト」, a neutral dark grey.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: layerling is free software (AGPL-3.0) and can be run on your own computer or server, for example in a workshop, a club or a school. There are several ways, described in the README on GitHub: The quick start on Windows: A single line in PowerShell installs everything and puts a shortcut on the desktop. When layerling is already running, another double-click starts no second server and only opens the page. Docker: For NAS devices and home servers, without Node.js needing to be installed. Every release comes as a ready-made image henmedia/layerling on Docker Hub (also ghcr.io/henmedia/layerling) for amd64 and arm64; docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v layerling-thumbnails:/app/.codex/project-thumbnails henmedia/layerling:latest starts it, and on a NAS you search for it in the container manager's registry. The volume layerling-thumbnails keeps the preview pictures of the start page through an update; without it they are missing each time the container is created again, until you open the design. Static export: The result is plain files that any web server can serve. They belong at the root of an address (https://layerling.example.com/ or http://192.168.0.5:8080/), not in a subfolder and not opened from disk; the README has the steps. With a writable folder store next to index.html and PHP on the server it also becomes the shared storage for designs. The MCP bridge for AI assistants exists only in the development server, see Building with an AI.

c: Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting
t: In the editor, the 「ヘルプ」 area holds the 「クイックガイド」 with the most important moves and the overview of keyboard shortcuts. Each section of the quick guide has a question mark that leads to the matching chapter here. The quick guide in the editor. Videos by others are listed at the top, and every section has a question mark. Questions, wishes and bug reports are welcome in the forum and on GitHub. What changed in which version is in the release notes, which you find at the bottom of the start page and of the editor.

Working with fingers or a stylus: selecting several bodies, turning and zooming the view, the long press menu, and what to know on an iPad.

layerling runs in the browser of a tablet, and as an app from its home screen. A finger does what the left mouse button does. Three things a tablet does not have, a right mouse button, a Shift key and a wheel, have a way of their own: You want to On a tablet Select a body Tap it. Select several bodies Tap a body: a round button appears in the lower left. Tap it, and every further body you tap joins the selection; a tap on a selected body takes it out again. A tap on empty space changes nothing; a second tap on the button ends it and clears the selection. Or hold a finger still for half a second, choose 「まとめて選ぶ」, then tap one body after another. Select all bodies Hold a finger still on empty space for half a second, choose 「すべて選択」. Open the menu of a right click Hold a finger still on a body or on empty space for half a second. Move a body Drag it. Resize, turn or lift a body Drag its handles, the small squares and arrows around it. A finger catches them from a little beside. Turn the view One finger on empty space, or drag the view cube. Zoom the view Two fingers: spread to come closer, pinch to go away. Move the view Slide two fingers together. Clear the selection Tap empty space. Not while 「1本指でビューを回転」 is on, where one finger turns the view; and in 「まとめて選ぶ」 the first tap on empty space only ends the mode and leaves the selection as it is, the next one clears it.

Without a Shift key, 「まとめて選ぶ」 in the menu of a long press does what Shift+click does on a computer. While it is on, a message says so, and each tap on a body adds it to the selection or takes it out again. A tap on empty space, or Esc on a keyboard, ends it and leaves the selection as it is. A finger on empty space still turns the view meanwhile. Then 「グループ化」, 「整列」 or a move work on all the bodies you picked. The same menu has 「面の上に置く」, the key C for a touch screen. The selection then follows the finger over the faces of other bodies; a tap sets it down on the face you tap, even a sloped one, and the first tap is enough. The menu entry is also found by searching for "set down" or "cruise" (the command search, Ctrl+K on a keyboard).

One finger on empty space turns the view, two fingers zoom and move it. A finger that starts on a body works on the body, not on the view. If you would rather have it turn the view, switch on 「1本指でビューを回転」 in the view bar: one finger then turns the view instead of selecting, wherever it starts. That switch only shows on a device with a touch screen. The view cube in the top left turns the view when you drag it, and a tap on one of its sides, corners or edges jumps to that view. See View and workplane.

h: Handles, small points and a stylus
t: A fingertip covers what it aims at. layerling lets a finger reach a little further to handles, points, lines and edges than a mouse pointer does, but a stylus is finer. This holds for a pen the tablet knows as a pen, such as an Apple Pencil or an S Pen. A plain stylus with a rubber tip counts as a finger for the screen and is not finer than one, so work with it as with a finger. An Apple Pencil that hovers above the screen on an iPad also shows the name of a control after a moment, in a small bubble, as the mouse pointer does with a tooltip. In sketch mode, 「Freehand」 draws with the pen or a finger as on paper; when you lift it, the line becomes sketch points you can edit, see Sketches. If bodies slip when children or hurried hands touch them, switch on 「移動の前に選択する」 in the settings: a body then has to be selected first, and only the next drag moves it.

Install it as an app. In Safari, tap the Share icon and choose "Add to Home Screen". The app opens in a window of its own without the address bar, and it works without a connection, see Offline and install. Your designs live in the browser (unless you host layerling yourself and set up a server folder). There is no account, and nothing is uploaded. Safari has a rule of its own against tracking: it deletes what a website stored after seven days in which you did not visit it in Safari. A web app added to the Home Screen is exempt from that rule, as WebKit documents it. That is one more reason to use the app from the Home Screen, and to back up important work: 「すべてバックアップ」 on the start page packs all designs into one file. Files. Safari lets a page write into a file only through a download, so 「エクスポート」 puts the file into the Downloads of the Files app, and Ctrl+S on a keyboard downloads it again; see Files and saving. No keyboard needed. Every tool has a button in the ribbon, and a number field opens the on-screen keyboard. A keyboard on the iPad adds the keyboard shortcuts. A value box beside a body opens its number field with the second tap: the first tap only marks it, so a finger that lands on it by accident does not raise the keyboard.

Fingers and rubber-tip styluses work alike here. Two settings make a class easier: 「移動の前に選択する」 so that a touch does not move a body by accident, and 「1本指でビューを回転」 so that one finger always turns the view. The question mark button in the Help group of the ribbon switches on the 「インタラクティブヘルプ」: a tap on any button, field or handle then explains it, and the same button, or Esc, leaves it. For a whole class, switch on 「かんたんモード」 in the settings. The ribbon then keeps only the tools a workshop uses (copy, paste, duplicate, delete, undo, group, mirror, chamfer, fillet, hollow, align, export), the shape library a short list, the buttons are larger, and the start page shows the designs and nothing else: no news, no welcome text, no help buttons and no links out of layerling. Switching it on is a tap; switching it off is a press held for two seconds on the button that then takes its place. A link ending in ?mode=simple switches it on for the device that opens it, ?mode=full switches it off again. Whoever runs layerling on a server can start everyone in it with LAYERLING_SIMPLE_MODE=true, or fix it for everyone with always, so that the program has no switch to leave it; see the README.
